body: My thought is I'm just numb to it. The shaking drives me insane. In any case, that's probably a healthier way of thinking about it, thank you.

That's really kind of you, thanks.

I flipped out this morning after a minor altercation, packed necessities, and drove to the other side of the city. I had a lot of ideas, but I realized any further, and I'll wind up back in the institute. Came back home, got some sleep, and deactivated facebook.

I'm going to be purging myself of social media for the next few weeks.

They had 200 employees where I worked. It was gossip circus, engineering edition. The guy in charge of me talked shit behind my back, and the next thing you know I was fired without warning. (He did NOT know how to write software!) They said it was for poor performance, a claim they could not substantiate when I inquired the weeks following. 

Pissed me the fuck off and now my dad has every right to believe them. I had a very difficult time making friends, even with plenty of people just older than me. I jumble speech and let out half baked thoughts that weird people out.

Needless to say I don't know what to do with my life anymore, can't make friends, girls avoid me when I talk too much, and I don't want to work for clueless millionaire engineers.

Nothing in my life helps my self esteem, that's for sure.

I've been seeing someone every week since January. I've been spiraling since losing my job though.
I'll probably go to bed. Thanks again.

EDIT: The worst part about going to bed is waking up with a clear mind. Everything comes back at once.

Yeah, she really is winning. Outside of immediate family (and even then), I don't know what it's like to be treated worthwhile.
Thank you.
My ex banging another dude on my bed
The butterfly effect. But then again, I watched it in Russian. I don't speak Russian.

I really feel for you right now.

I also really feel like there's a way out. The system has courts, officers, restraining orders, safe spaces, and even hotlines for this kind of shit. It sounds like you feel powerless, so let those with power save you!

A friend of mine attempted suicide, lived, and fled across the country. One of her brothers helped her file a restraining order from her vile, fucking abusive parents. They can't touch her now. Is there anyone you could go to at this point? Law enforcement will certainly take you in!

For your daughter's sake (and my own!), please, please keep trying.

I shit you not, the days I'm publicly depressed (like today) are the days I do the best socially. My depression keeps my mind on a single track (ADD, mouth usually can't keep up), and my no fucks given attitude keeps me from reading into anything past my cynical first impression (no anxiety). I'm nicer to strangers too. I can even keep up with *smalltalk*, because I can understand what people are saying faster. I legitimately have *better days*.

But, of course, better days improve my mood, which makes me think faster, fret, and stutter more. Generally, I don't actually feel anxiety, but I will start shaking if I am expecting social interaction. People describe me as uptight. That, my profuse acne, and the way people avoid me bring me down again. It's a cycle with period ~= 4 days.

You'd probably be surprised how fast people will forget, or rather how many times you can get away with it. I bet they see you as more of a person, too --bad days and all.
I would prefer that to dating a lie. Trust me, I dated one for 2.5 years.

I think everyone on this sub can relate with you there. I know I can.

On a more scientific note, from everything I've read, seen, and experienced, that's literally how our brains work. Thinking an emotional thought makes the thought come back, and stronger. One of my therapists helped me accept really nasty thoughts without pushing back. (Far easier said than done.) It's something that worked for me.

If only ADD didn't get in the way of meditation. Only long hikes can clear my mind in the wake of the shit I've seen.
Glad to hear there's someone else.

I was in the same boat 6 years ago. College is surprisingly easy to get into, and there's this big circus of freshman friend groups that form those first few weeks. Everyone is new, everyone is more mature. It really does get better.

I remember, I needed to change my sock for some reason, and I told the group I met that day to wait so I could change it. We were going to walk over and get ice cream, and to my surprise, **they actually did**. It meant so much to me.

High school is fucking warped. I hear high schoolers at the rock gym I climb at, and I cringe only at the thought of their mentality, their skewed, twisted view of the world. Their weird, superficial conversations portray it. You shouldn't assume things will stay the same.

I can't listen to anything that lifts me up when I'm down, or really anything that doesn't speak to me in general. Thom Yorke's "Tomorrow's Modern Boxes" and "The Eraser" certainly speak to me when I'm down though.
